rules.why: Coverage reaches ordinary residential tenancies subject only to small owner-occupied, hotel/seasonal, and special trust exclusions, and no effective date is given.
Coverage turns on the building-specific construction-completion date because only newly constructed multiple dwellings within 30 years are exempt, and no effective date is given.
The rule broadly covers ordinary apartment rentals with only small owner-occupied, transient/seasonal, and special trust exclusions, and no effective date is given.
Residential security deposits are broadly covered, with only seasonal-rental and small-landlord handling distinctions, and no effective date is given.
The cap covers ordinary multifamily rental applications while excluding one- and two-family dwellings and certain licensees, and the stated date is when the new act takes effect.
The rule broadly covers rental dwelling units except owner-occupied premises of four or fewer units, and the stated date is when the act takes effect.
The antidiscrimination rule broadly covers landlord-tenant rentals with only owner-occupied, single-sex, and age-restricted exceptions, and no effective date is given.
The ban covers ordinary residential dwelling units used as primary residences with facility-type exclusions, and the stated date is when the new act takes effect.
